name: Krishang Reddy Mandala
affiliations: UT Dallas · JURS Independent Research Study
summary: Undergraduate computer science researcher at UT Dallas, tracing the lineage of Situational AI and how Endsley's model of situation awareness shows up in AI systems.

sections.heading: About
sections.html:
Krishang Reddy Mandala is a junior reading for a B.S. in Computer Science at UT Dallas and a Jindal Undergraduate Research Scholar. He is working on the Situational AI position paper and framework.

His contribution is the lineage: several research traditions have each solved part of this problem — McCarthy's situation calculus gave a formal way to describe how actions change the world, context-aware computing built software that adapts to its surroundings, and robotics connected sensing, understanding and prediction. Situational AI brings the same question to language-based agents. His working claim is that having the right information is not the same as understanding what is happening.

He presents The Evolution at the October 22 forum.

sections.heading: Research interests
sections.html:
• Endsley's three-level model of situation awareness — perception, comprehension, projection — and what transfers to AI
  • Situation calculus, context-aware computing and robotics as the intellectual lineage of the idea
  • The situation as a first-class, explainable object a system can hold and show its evidence for
  • The difference between context engineering and understanding
  • Benchmarking a situation-centric system against existing systems
  • Stating the position formally enough that others can take it up or refute it

name: Sabareesh Dinakaran
affiliations: UT Dallas · JURS Independent Research Study
summary: Undergraduate researcher at UT Dallas asking whether recognizing the situation first lets an AI system spend far less computation.

sections.heading: About
sections.html:
Sabareesh Dinakaran is a student at UT Dallas, a Jindal Undergraduate Research Scholar, and spent the summer as an intern at Mindspace AI.

His work treats the hypothesis as an efficiency question. Tokens are the meter: cost and energy track token count, and an agentic multi-step task can consume anywhere from fifteen thousand to over a million tokens where a chat reply uses two hundred. Because models are stateless, every prompt regenerates the same context, producing redundant processing and runaway loops. His argument is that a stored situation object allows incremental updates instead of full-sequence inference — which is what would make small, local, specialized models viable.

He presents The Computation at the October 22 forum.

sections.heading: Research interests
sections.html:
• Token consumption as the practical meter of cost and energy in AI systems
  • What stateless inference costs when every prompt regenerates its own context
  • Situation memory as an alternative to re-reading context, and incremental updates over full-sequence inference
  • Whether an explicit situation layer makes small, local and specialized models viable
  • The energy and water footprint of data-centre inference against local hardware
  • Deciding whether computation is warranted before spending it

name: Sai Jagadish Manchikanti
affiliations: UT Dallas · JURS Independent Research Study
summary: Undergraduate researcher at UT Dallas building RiskPulse, which asks whether situation recognition can improve risk decisions in small and mid-sized businesses.

sections.heading: About
sections.html:
Sai Jagadish Manchikanti is a junior at UT Dallas majoring in Computer Information Systems & Technology and Finance, on a pre-PhD track, and a Jindal Undergraduate Research Scholar. He has competed in a sustainability competition with Infosys on supply chain management and AI, and is writing a research paper with Prof. Ramesh Subramoniam and Prasad Pillai.

He built RiskPulse to test the hypothesis against real organizational risk. His observation is that risk lives in combinations rather than in single alerts: the largest customer thirty days late, payroll still due and suppliers still to fund is one cash situation, not three notifications. RiskPulse retrieves the records, calculates the metrics with checked formulas, has the model explain the implications, and leaves the choice of path to a person.

He presents The Experiments, with a live demo, at the October 22 forum.

sections.heading: Research interests
sections.html:
• Emerging organizational risk, and why it appears in combinations of signals rather than in single alerts
  • Situation recognition for small and mid-sized businesses, where there is no analyst to join the dots
  • Dividing the work: retrieval for records, checked formulas for the numbers, the model for explanation, the person for the decision
  • Keeping a human in the loop on consequential financial choices
  • Supply chain management and AI
  • How a recognized situation shapes which response is appropriate — collect, prioritize, compare, monitor

name: Yuvan Muruganandham
affiliations: UT Dallas · JURS Independent Research Study
summary: Honors computer science student at UT Dallas and the creator of Sentinel, which turns a fraud alert into an inspectable situation rather than a verdict.

sections.heading: About
sections.html:
Yuvan Muruganandham is an honors computer science student at UT Dallas, a Jindal Undergraduate Research Scholar, and a machine learning engineering intern at Mindspace AI. He is the creator of Sentinel.

Sentinel applies situation recognition to card-not-present fraud triage, on the principle that an alert is an event and not yet an answer. It turns an alert into candidate situation types and shows the evidence for and against each one; the optional local language model writes narrative only and cannot choose a label, a prediction set or an action. Unresolved cases route to senior review rather than being called benign, a person decides, and every step lands in a hash-chained audit trail.

He presents The Experiments, with a live demo, at the October 22 forum.

sections.heading: Research interests
sections.html:
• Turning alerts into inspectable situations, with the evidence for and against each candidate made visible
  • Keeping language generation outside the decision path — narration without decision authority
  • Prediction sets and policy as the route from a recognized situation to a proposed action
  • Restraint as a design feature: routing the unresolved to human review rather than resolving it
  • Auditability, so an assessment and the analyst's disposition can be reconstructed afterwards
  • Reporting negative results honestly, and treating evidence quality as the thing to fix before automation

name: Avani Tripathi
affiliations: UT Dallas · JURS Independent Research Study

documents.title: Does Situational AI Represent an Emerging Programming Paradigm?
documents.meta: Situations as the Core Abstraction for Reasoning, Decision-Making, and Execution · Avani Tripathi · UT Dallas · JURS Independent Research Study, 2026

documents.title: Situational AI: An Emerging Programming Paradigm
documents.meta: Slides accompanying the literature review · 13 slides

summary: Undergraduate researcher at UT Dallas asking whether situation, rather than the prompt, is becoming the unit an intelligent system should reason from.

sections.heading: About
sections.html:
Avani Tripathi is an undergraduate researcher at the Naveen Jindal School of Management, UT Dallas, and a Jindal Undergraduate Research Scholar. She joined the Situational AI inquiry in 2026 through the JURS programme and spent the summer as an intern at Mindspace AI.

Her work approaches Situational AI as a question about software itself. For most of the history of programming, a system's behaviour has been settled before it runs — by explicit control flow, by class hierarchies, later by a learned distribution. Her research asks what changes when the situation becomes the thing a system reasons from, and whether that amounts to a new paradigm rather than a new technique.

She opens the October 22 forum with The Idea.

sections.heading: Research interests
sections.html:
• Programming paradigms and how they succeed one another — procedural, object-oriented, machine-learned, agentic
  • Whether situation can serve as a core computational abstraction, and how it differs from a prompt, a task, a context window or a workflow
  • The architecture of agentic and AI-native systems, and the distinction between orchestration and understanding
  • Situational awareness as intellectual lineage, from Endsley's three-stage model to shared awareness in human–autonomous teams
  • Human–AI teaming: escalation, hand-off, and keeping machine reasoning legible for human review
  • How a situation-centric system could be evaluated empirically against an agentic baseline

sections.html: As Director of Undergraduate Research at the Naveen Jindal School of Management, Prof. Subramoniam directs the Jindal Undergraduate Research Scholars (JURS) program through which five UT Dallas students carried out independent research studies on Situational AI in 2026. He opens the October 22 forum and is recognized in its closing segment.

name: Prasad Pillai
summary: Initiated the Situational AI inquiry after two decades building software and, most recently, AI coworkers. Responsible for the hypothesis and the research program.

sections.heading: About
sections.html: Prasad Pillai initiated Situational AI and is responsible for its hypothesis and research program. He is the founder and CEO of Mindspace AI, the organizational and engineering home of the work, and the founder of BotsWork, where situation-centric ideas are being tested in working AI coworker systems.

sections.heading: Why I Started This Inquiry
sections.html:
The inquiry began with a practical frustration. Modern AI had become remarkably good at reasoning once it was told what problem to solve. Given the right prompt and the right context, it could write, plan, analyze and explain. And yet the systems we were building still failed in ordinary situations, not because they reasoned badly but because nobody had told them what was going on.

Real work does not arrive as prompts. A customer goes quiet. A payment fails for a long-standing account. A project drifts. Nobody asks anything; something changes. The harder problem was recognizing what problem exists, for whom it matters, and what the moment calls for. That question, once noticed, was hard to put down.

sections.heading: From Building AI Coworkers to Situation Recognition
sections.html:
Building AI coworkers at BotsWork made the gap concrete. Giving an agent more context helped, up to a point. What it could not do was tell an ordinary card decline from a valuable customer being blocked by a temporary outage, or a cooling prospect from a resolved support ticket, when the underlying data looked the same. Smart was not the same as competent.

The pattern kept repeating: the missing capability was not more knowledge or better reasoning but recognition, an explicit account of the situation the system was in, from whose perspective, and what that implied. That led from context engineering to situation recognition, and from there to the question of whether situations should be first-class objects in the architecture rather than something inferred and forgotten inside each prompt.

sections.heading: The Situational AI Hypothesis
sections.html: Situation deserves to become a first-class computational primitive of intelligent systems: something a system detects, represents, compares, tracks, remembers and revises as evidence changes. Situation is to intelligent behavior what the token is to language modeling, an analogy about computational role, not a claim that the work is done. The manifesto sets the hypothesis out in full; the research program is the attempt to test it.

sections.heading: Current Research Questions
sections.html:
• Can a system recognize which situation is emerging from changing evidence, and notice when its interpretation is wrong?
  • Can experience be remembered as situations, responses and outcomes rather than as text?
  • Can structurally analogous situations be found across domains that share no vocabulary?
  • Does an explicit situation layer actually improve timing, decision quality, coordination and explanation?

These are the open questions of the program, not settled results.

sections.heading: Professional Background
sections.html: Over two decades of building technology to solve real-world problems, including roles at Microsoft and co-founding Elsys Intelligent Devices. Founder and CEO of Mindspace AI, which conducts applied AI research, proofs of concept and engineering around emerging AI architectures; founder of BotsWork. Speaker, including a TEDx talk, with coverage in The Better India, Manorama News, Crazy Engineers, Mathrubhumi News and Raksha Net.
